talks.title: The past is prologue: Intel needs to evolve to survive
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning The past is prologue: Intel needs to evolve to survive.
talks.summary:
Overview: Vizzy, founder of the Vertex Project and co-author of the original APT1 report, presents at HITCON on intelligence analysis evolution and why the discipline must adapt to survive.

Key Topics: The APT1 report's origins at Mandiant in 2013; Chinese espionage targeting aerospace, pharmaceutical, and technology sectors; existential threats from stolen R&D; and the future of cyber threat intelligence analysis.

Technical Details: Vizzy recounts identifying Unit 61398's multi-year campaign exfiltrating terabytes weekly from English-speaking businesses, from aerospace engine schematics to pharmaceutical research. The report established attribution methodology now standard in CTI.

Takeaways: CTI must evolve beyond indicator sharing to strategic analysis of adversary intent and impact. The APT1 model of public attribution changed the industry, but analysts must continue adapting methodologies.

talks.title: ARTIPHISHELL Agents: LLM-Driven Bug Hunting & Patching in Open Source Software
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for ARTIPHISHELL Agents: LLM-Driven Bug Hunting & Patching in Open Source Software.
talks.summary:
DARPA AI Cyber Challenge

Will Gibbs and Lucas Dresl of the Shellphish multi-university team present their HITCON talk on LLM-driven autonomous bug hunting and patching for open source, built for DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge with roughly twenty-six contributors from ASU, UCSB, and Purdue.

Competition scope

AIC targets fully autonomous discovery and repair across hard codebases such as nginx, SQLite, Jenkins, and the Linux kernel. Semifinalists received two-million-dollar prizes; finals added larger awards. Motivations included prize money, giving back to open source, and learning bleeding-edge LLM security uses.

Pipeline overview

Their CRS narrows huge codebases using Semgrep and CodeQL queries, prioritizing delta-mode diffs where new changes introduce or expose bugs. Diffy generates targeted CodeQL queries around patches; Code Swipe heuristically weights candidate functions from diff proximity, static warnings, and reachability before LLMs analyze prioritized code for exploitable issues.
